description.en: Steady rain on a cabin roof in the forest, with distant thunder rolling through now and then.

beds.csvNotes: 44.1 kHz/32-float master, resampled by the pipeline; 4.5 dB decay across the take flattened before looping
beds.notes: 60 s from 0 s with a 2 s crossfade (only 62.2 s of source exists, so this is the longest loop that leaves a full crossfade of tail). The take is recorded very quietly (peak -35.8 dBFS, 5 s RMS falling from -60 to -64.5 dB), so flattenDrift levels it toward the median before the fold; without it the loop breathes ~4.5 dB every minute. Bands are even across 120 Hz-8 kHz (no tonal peaks), which is what a rain bed needs. The take peaks at -35.8 dBFS with droplet attacks ~26 dB above the bed, so after the +34 dB normalisation the loudest drops sat at -2 dBFS with a 25 dB crest and read as sizzle: a -10 dBFS limiter with a 40 ms release pulls the crest back before the final normalise
